notes: First major formation of the division in Normandy: 32nd (Guards) Infantry Brigade landed and attached 28 June to 43rd Division for Epsom (division landed 28 June per Wikipedia list).

current_activity: Goodwood: the Grenadier Guards and the 32nd Guards Brigade clear Cagny by about 19:30 after a day of fighting
notes: Event date: 18 July 1944 (Ellis, vol. I, pp. 342, 343). Event definition: The Guards Armoured Division, following the 11th Armoured Division across the Orne, is held up on the left flank between Emieville and Cagny; the 2nd Armoured Grenadier Guards with infantry of the 32nd Guards Brigade are well into Cagny by 18:00 and clear it about an hour and a half later (pp. 341-343). Event support: one source family (Ellis, the British official history). Ellis, Victory in the West, vol. I, p. 342: "The 2nd Armoured Grenadiers, with infantry of the 32nd Guards Brigade, were well into the village by six o"; p. 343: "and had cleared it completely about an hour and a half later". Location: Cagny, Calvados (existing place PL0529) with a precision of 3 km. Location support: Ellis names Cagny as the village taken by the division (pp. 342-343).

current_activity: Bluecoat: ordered up on the left of the 11th Armoured Division; leading troops are south-east of St. Martin by evening
notes: Event date: 31 July 1944 (Ellis, vol. I, p. 394). Event definition: On learning of the 11th Armoured Division's success at the Souleuvre, VIII Corps orders the Guards Armoured Division, waiting north of Caumont, to come up on the 11th's left and secure more routes over the river near Le Tourneur; by evening its leading troops reach the hills south-east of St. Martin-des-Besaces, strongly held by the 21st Panzer Division, and the attack on Point 192 fails that night (p. 394). Event support: one source family (Ellis, the British official history). Ellis, Victory in the West, vol. I, p. 394: "on learning of the 11th Armoured's success at the Souleuvre, General O'Connor ordered the Guards Armoured Division (then waiting north of Caumont) to come up on the 11th's left and secure additional routes over the river in the neighbourhood of le Tourneur"; "By evening the leading troops of the division had reached the hills south-east of St. Martin to find them strongly held by tanks and infantry of the 21st Panzer Division". Location: Saint-Martin-des-Besaces, Calvados (new place) with a precision of 5 km. Location approximate: the point is St. Martin-des-Besaces; the hills reached lie a short distance south-east of it. Location support: Ellis names the hills south-east of St. Martin as reached by the division (p. 394).

current_activity: Guards cross the Somme seven or eight miles east of Amiens; armoured cars save the bridges at midday, bridgehead by dark
notes: Event date: 31 August 1944 (Ellis, vol. I, pp. 469, 470). Event definition: The division is across the Somme seven or eight miles east of Amiens on the 31st: its armoured cars reach the river about midday in time to save the bridges, tanks and infantry settle the issue and by dark it holds a substantial bridgehead, some ninety miles from where it had started at two o'clock that morning (pp. 469-470). Event support: one source family (Ellis, the British official history). Ellis, Victory in the West, vol. I, pp. 469-470: "The Guards Armoured Division was also across the Somme, seven or eight miles further east"; "By dark the Guards held a substantial bridgehead". Location: Amiens, Somme (new place), standing for the Somme crossing east of the town with a precision of 10 km. Location approximate: the point is Amiens; the bridgehead lies seven or eight miles to the east, along the river. Location support: Ellis places the division seven or eight miles east of Amiens (p. 469).

current_activity: Dash for Brussels: reaches the city in the early evening of 3 September; the population is in the streets
notes: Event date: 3 September 1944, early evening (Ellis, vol. II, pp. 4, 5). Event definition: XXX Corps is ordered about midnight on 2 September to advance on Brussels and Antwerp as early as possible; on 3 September the Guards Armoured Division, with the 231st Infantry Brigade from the 50th Division under its command, advances on two routes: the 32nd Guards Brigade (Welsh Guards group) by Ath and Hal and the 5th Guards Brigade (Grenadier group) by Lessines and Ninove; the Household Cavalry scout cars are the first to reach the city boundary, the Grenadiers are delayed at the outskirts, and the Welsh Guards are the first to enter in force in the early evening (pp. 4-5). Event support: one source family (Ellis, the British official history). Ellis, Victory in the West, vol. II, p. 4: "About midnight XXX Corps was ordered to advance on Brussels and Antwerp starting as early as possible"; p. 5: "when Brussels was reached in the early evening the whole population was in the streets". Location: Brussels, Belgium (new place) with a precision of 5 km. Location approximate: the point is the centre of Brussels, the objective reached; the division headquarters is not named. Location support: Ellis names Brussels as reached by the division in the early evening (p. 5). Commander: Lt.-Gen. B. G. Horrocks, who succeeded Lt.-Gen. G. C. Bucknall in command of XXX Corps on 4 August 1944 (Ellis, vol. I, p. 400; named again on pp. 453 and 469).

current_activity: Nijmegen: with the 82nd Airborne Division takes the road and rail bridges over the Waal after a day of hard fighting
notes: Event date: 20 September 1944 (Ellis, vol. II, p. 39). Event definition: On 20 September part of the Guards Armoured Division and of the 82nd Airborne Division resume the attack on the Nijmegen bridges; the road bridge approach is taken after hard fighting lasting all day, paratroops cross the Waal about a mile downstream in canvas boats provided by the Guards, and tanks of the Grenadier Guards then burst across the road bridge and join the Americans on the north bank (p. 39). Event support: one source family (Ellis, the British official history). Ellis, Victory in the West, vol. II, p. 39: "Guards Armoured Division resumed their attack for the capture of the Nijmegen bridges"; "tanks of the Grenadier Guards burst across the road bridge (in spite of fire from snipers in the super-structure and '88' guns posted to cover it) and joined the Americans coming to meet them on the north bank". Location: Nijmegen, Gelderland (existing place PL0554) with a precision of 3 km. Location approximate: the point is Nijmegen, where the Waal bridges stand; the division headquarters is not named. Location support: Ellis names the Nijmegen road and rail bridges over the Waal (p. 39). Commander: Lt.-Gen. B. G. Horrocks, who succeeded Lt.-Gen. G. C. Bucknall in command of XXX Corps on 4 August 1944 (Ellis, vol. I, p. 400; named again on pp. 453 and 469).

current_activity: Rhineland: passes through the 3rd Division; stiff fighting at Kapellen; captures Bonninghardt and the commanding ground
notes: Event date: 6 March 1945, by the evening (Ellis, vol. II, p. 276). Event definition: As XXX Corps' drive wheels sharply to the north-east, the Guards Armoured Division, now in action as a division, is to pass through the British 3rd Division for Kapellen and the hills around Bonninghardt; by the evening of 6 March the Guards, after stiff fighting at Kapellen and in the woods to the east, capture Bonninghardt and its commanding ground; by 9 March the division has broken Schlemm's lateral road near Menzelen after a very stiff battle (p. 276). Event support: one source family (Ellis, the British official history). Ellis, Victory in the West, vol. II, p. 276: "on its left the Guards Armoured, now in action as a division, was to pass through the British 3rd Division for Kapellen and the hills around Bonninghardt"; "The Guards, after stiff fighting at Kapellen and in the woods to the east, captured Bonninghardt and its commanding ground". Location: Bönninghardt, North Rhine-Westphalia (new place), the hills and ridge captured with a precision of 3 km. Location approximate: the point is the Bönninghardt ridge near Alpen; the division headquarters is not named. Location support: Ellis names Bonninghardt and its commanding ground as the objective captured (p. 276).

current_activity: Advance to the Elbe: XXX Corps spearhead, started on 30 March, reaches Enschede on 1 April
notes: Event date: 1 April 1945 (the corps started from the Rhine bridgehead on 30 March) (Ellis, vol. II, p. 307). Event definition: XXX Corps, on the left flank, starts from the Rhine bridgehead on 30 March with the Guards Armoured Division in the lead; the division reaches Enschede at the end of the Twente canal on 1 April after a number of minor tussles with German rearguards and from there takes two roads with a brigade on each; on the right a tough fight against a group of the German 8th Parachute Division delays it short of Bentheim, which is secured only on 4 April (p. 307). Event support: one source family (Ellis, the British official history). Ellis, Victory in the West, vol. II, p. 307: "on the left flank, had started from the Rhine bridgehead on the joth of March with the Guards Armoured Division in the lead"; "They reached Enschede at the end of the Twente canal on the 1st of April after a number of minor tussles with German rearguards". Location: Enschede, Overijssel (new place) with a precision of 3 km. Location approximate: the point is the town centre of Enschede; the division headquarters is not named. Location support: Ellis names Enschede as the town reached (p. 307).

current_activity: Advance to the Elbe: reaches the Ems at Lingen by 04:00; a Coldstream group takes an intact bridge below
notes: Event date: 3 April 1945 (Ellis, vol. II, p. 307). Event definition: On the main Arnhem-Bremen road the left brigade of the Guards Armoured Division makes a ten-mile midnight dash with full headlights for Lingen on the Ems and reaches the river by 04:00 on 3 April, but the enemy blows the bridge as they arrive; after daylight a Household Cavalry patrol finds an intact bridge three miles downstream with a road block covered by three 88-mm guns and prepared for demolition, and a Coldstream Guards group detached to capture it does so with the bridge intact under Captain Ian Liddell, who is awarded the Victoria Cross (p. 307). Event support: one source family (Ellis, the British official history). Ellis, Victory in the West, vol. II, p. 307: "By 4 a.m. on the 3rd the Ems was reached but the enemy blew the bridge as they arrived"; "a Coldstream Guards group was detached to capture it and did so, with the bridge intact". Location: Lingen (Ems), Niedersachsen (new place) with a precision of 5 km. Location approximate: the point is the town centre of Lingen; the intact bridge was about three miles (5 km) downstream and the division headquarters is not named. Location support: Ellis names Lingen and the Ems bridge three miles downstream (p. 307).

current_activity: Bremen: to the north captures Zeven and frees 8,000 British and Allied prisoners at Westertimke
notes: Event date: by 27 April 1945 (the page gives no day for Zeven) (Ellis, vol. II, pp. 309, 316). Event definition: While XXX Corps closes in on Bremen, the Guards Armoured Division, which Dempsey has ordered to move from XXX Corps to XII Corps as operations progress (p. 309), captures Zeven to the north-east of the city and frees 8,000 British and Allied prisoners, mostly sailors, from a camp at Westertimke nearby; the page gives no day for the capture (it is in the account of the days to the 27th) (p. 316). Event support: one source family (Ellis, the British official history). Ellis, Victory in the West, vol. II, p. 316: "To the north the Guards Armoured Division had captured Zeven and freed 8,000 British and Allied prisoners, mostly sailors, from a camp at Westertimke nearby"; p. 309: "and the Guards Armoured Division to move from XXX Corps to XII Corps". Location: Zeven, Niedersachsen (new place) with a precision of 3 km. Location approximate: the point is the town centre of Zeven; the camp at Westertimke is a few kilometres away and the division headquarters is not named. Location support: Ellis names Zeven and the camp at Westertimke (p. 316).
